annotation.speech2: A semicircle drawn on a horizontal diameter of length a plus b, with a equal to 4 on the left and b equal to 1 on the right, meeting at the point D. The center of the semicircle is O. Three segments in the picture have lengths equal to the three means of a and b. A red vertical segment from O up to the top of the arc is the radius, whose length is the arithmetic mean 2.5. A blue vertical segment from D up to the point C on the arc is the altitude of the inscribed right triangle, whose length is the geometric mean 2. A purple segment along the radius O C, running from C back to the foot M of the perpendicular dropped from D, has length equal to the harmonic mean 1.6. Because a leg of a right triangle is never longer than its hypotenuse, the harmonic mean is at most the geometric mean, which is at most the arithmetic mean.
The semicircle whose diameter is the segment of length a plus b, that is, of length 5.
The diameter, split at the point D into a left piece of length a equal to 4 and a right piece of length b equal to 1.
The arithmetic mean, drawn in red: the vertical radius from the center O to the top of the arc, of length a plus b over 2, which is 2.5.
The geometric mean, drawn in blue: the vertical segment from D up to the point C on the arc, of length the square root of a b, which is 2.
The harmonic mean, drawn in purple: the piece of the radius O C running from C back to M, of length 2 a b over a plus b, which is 1.6.
The chord from the left end of the diameter to the point C on the arc, one leg of the inscribed right triangle, drawn in gray.
The chord from C to the right end of the diameter, the other leg of the inscribed right triangle, drawn in gray.

The right angle marker at C: any triangle inscribed in a semicircle has a right angle at the point on the arc, which is why the blue segment is an altitude from a right angle and therefore the geometric mean.
The radius from the center O out to the point C on the arc. Its length is also the arithmetic mean 2.5, and the purple harmonic mean is the part of it nearest C.
The perpendicular dropped from D to the radius O C, meeting it at the point M.
The right angle marker at M, showing that D M is perpendicular to the radius O C.
